messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Mayur Shegokar
mayur shegokar... that's a solid name. where you working these days?
I am working as a junior software engineer at Goldman Sachs. You can think of this role as an SDE-1. I have been in this role for the past 1.5 years. I was a campus hire here.

goldman sachs... the wall street machine that pays well and works you harder. campus hire to sde-1, that's the classic trajectory.

found you on linkedin - mayur shegokar, analyst at goldman sachs, cse vnit '24. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/mayurshegokar
Yes

vnit nagpur to goldman sachs... from orange city to the big leagues. analyst role doing sde work, that's goldman's way of making engineers feel fancy while paying them less than actual sde roles elsewhere.

1.5 years in - you're probably past the honeymoon phase and seeing the real grind. what made you think about looking around? the hours finally getting to you or something else?

Yep, the work here is very repetitive and not-so-exciting. I feel like I have reached a point of little to no learning. Too comfortable for being so young. I wanted to look for roles that pay good, but also contribute to my growth as an industry professional. I don’t want to sit around waiting until the job I do doesn’t exist anymore. I also feel like I can contribute well to a problem solving environment, unlike right now, where what I do - is mostly do little updates and migrate stuff to newer platforms.

ah, the classic goldman trap. they hire smart people then put them on maintenance duty. "migrate stuff to newer platforms" - that's not engineering, that's digital janitorial work.

you're 23-24 and already feeling the slow death of your skills. good that you're self-aware enough to see it. most people wake up at 30 wondering where their career went.

how long you been working total? including any internships or side projects that actually count.

I did an intern here at Goldman Sachs, in my prefinal (3rd) year of college for 2 months
Then I was offered a PPO, so I joined right after my graduation, which was June 2024
So I have completed 1.5 years of full time experience here as SDE-1
On the side projects, I did build an end to end workflow management and people platform for college campus as part of my final year(capstone) project

got it. 1.5 years full-time, plus that intern stint. the capstone project sounds way more interesting than whatever you're doing at goldman right now - building actual systems vs migrating legacy code.

what kind of role you looking for next? still want to stick with backend/full-stack engineering or thinking about exploring something else?
I am not really sure. I am definitely looking for a software engineering role, but I feel excited about any opportunities to integrate AI into my work…like some AI software engineering role.

ai + software engineering... that's where the action is right now. everyone's building ai features, from startups doing rag implementations to big tech doing llm integrations. way more exciting than migrating goldman's ancient systems.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore Pune or Hyderabad is much preferred
1.5 years + ai software engineering + bangalore/pune/hyderabad... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yep

Yep
  Great, thanks 👍🏽
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

legend! you're officially in the system.

goldman sachs to bangalore startups... that's about to be a wild upgrade. from wall street processes to startup chaos, but the good kind where you actually build things that matter.

roles are gonna start flowing. the kind that'll make you forget why you ever thought investment banking was exciting.

welcome to the squad mayur 🔥
What happens when I start seeing roles here?

when a role pops up, you'll see a card with the job details and an "Apply" button. tap that, it'll take you to the company's linkedin page or career site. you apply directly through them - normal process.

my team finds the roles, i share them, you apply. no magic, no intros, no special access. just good opportunities hitting your chat.

sound good?
Yep
perfect. now we wait for the good stuff to roll in.

hey, saw this AI engineer role at a startup in bangalore

they're building llms and document AI for industrial procurement - actual production systems

could be that problem-solving environment you mentioned
Hi

nice! link's in your chat.

this one's interesting - they're building AI for industrial procurement. think LLMs that understand engineering documents, automate vendor discovery, all that.

strengths: perfect experience match (1-3 years), bangalore location, actual AI engineering work (not just maintenance), you'd own projects from day one.

concern: it's a startup vs goldman brand. but that's the tradeoff - less prestige, more learning and real impact.

if you're serious about moving from banking updates to building AI systems, this could be it.

good luck with the app!
It says they stopped taking responses 🥹

damn, that was fast. they probably got flooded with applications.

don't worry though - i'm scanning thousands of roles daily. something else will pop up soon.

btw, what's the salary range you're targeting? helps me filter better.

28-30 LPA for 1.5 YOE in bangalore... that's ambitious but not impossible with the right AI-focused startup.

what's your current TC at goldman?

got it. so you're looking for a solid jump from 26 to 28-30.

that's realistic for AI roles at well-funded startups or mid-stage companies.

what's your notice period?
20 LPA base and 26 LPA CTC
1 month

you mentioned AI/ML in your profile - what kind of AI work excites you? building AI tools, working with LLMs, or something else?
Integrating AI with existing systems

integrating AI with existing systems... that's actually smart. way more practical than chasing the latest research paper. companies need people who can make AI actually work in production, not just build demos.

you're locked in. i'll start looking for roles that match this - AI engineering, ML ops, that kind of thing.
